title: ResolvedOrder
description: What the signal-processing backend publishes to the Redis stream 'orders.resolved' for the execution system to consume. This is the seam between signal-processing and execution - treat changes as an API version bump. No quantity field on purpose: execution computes its own position size from settings.capital_per_trade / risk_per_trade_pct / price at open time, rather than signal-generation/signal-processing deciding capital exposure - see docs/architecture.md. stop_loss_method/stop_loss_interval/stop_loss_percent/target_percent/trailing_stop_enabled/duplicate_signal_policy/counter_signal_policy are passed through unchanged from the resolved Strategy (signal-generation) - execution uses them to compute stop_loss_price/target_price, size/monitor the position, and resolve same-symbol signal conflicts, but never calls signal-generation directly to get them. No square_off_time field here on purpose either - square-off is a per-segment setting owned entirely by execution (execution.accounts.square_off_time, editable via PUT /accounts/{segment}), not a per-Strategy one, so execution never needs signal-processing to hand it one - see docs/architecture.md.

strategy_id.description: Which signal-generation Strategy produced this order - carried through from signal-ingest unchanged. Not to be confused with the 'strategy' field below (option-strategy legs, e.g. bull_call_spread).

exchange.description: Carried through from signal-ingest unchanged - tells execution which quote provider owns this position's CMP. 'CRYPTO' is Delta Exchange India (market-data's DeltaProvider) - see docs/architecture.md.

segment.description: From the resolved Strategy (signal-generation.strategies.segment, always set, defaults NSE) - tells execution which execution.accounts row (one per segment) to size against and credit/debit on close. A different axis from exchange in principle, but each segment maps to exactly one exchange today (NSE<->NSE, MCX<->MCX, CRYPTO<->CRYPTO), so they always co-occur 1:1.

strategy.description: Option-strategy legs (spread/straddle/etc) - unrelated to strategy_id above. Populated by signal-processing's choose_strategy (Phase 4b of the options trading module, see docs/architecture.md) for instrument_type='option' orders; null for spot/future orders. Actioned by execution as a combined-SL 2-leg position (Phase 4d), see docs/architecture.md.

type.description: Which fixed template produced these legs, e.g. 'bull_call_spread'/'bear_put_spread' - a plain string, not an enum yet, so a new template doesn't need a contract change.

security_id.description: The option contract's own provider-assigned ID (Dhan's security ID for NSE/MCX, Delta Exchange India's product_id for CRYPTO - from market-data's option-chain response either way). Resolved to a trading symbol/lot size by execution at position-open time via market-data's GET /instruments/resolve-by-security-id (Phase 4d), see docs/architecture.md.

price.description: Price at signal trigger time, carried through unchanged - execution uses this directly as the paper-trade entry price.

stop_loss_method.description: From the resolved Strategy. null means no stop-loss configured - execution falls back to plain capital_per_trade sizing with no stop/target monitoring. 'breakeven' (added 2026-08-29): a one-shot variant of 'percent' - opens with the identical initial stop, but once price first moves stop_loss_percent% favorably from entry, the stop snaps to entry_price and freezes there (execution.positions.breakeven_triggered records the one-shot state).

stop_loss_interval.description: Set when stop_loss_method='previous_candle' (the candle interval execution asks market-data's GET /candles/previous for) or stop_loss_method='indicator' (the candle interval execution asks market-data's GET /candles/history for).

stop_loss_percent.description: Set when stop_loss_method='percent' or 'breakeven' - for 'breakeven' this is both the initial stop distance and the favorable-move trigger threshold.

stop_loss_indicator_type.description: Only set when stop_loss_method='indicator' - which computation to run ('ema' or 'supertrend' today). See signal-generation's app/domain/rule.py _STOP_LOSS_INDICATOR_PARAMS_MODELS and execution's app/domain/position_manager.py _STOP_LOSS_COMPUTE_FUNCS - both must be widened together when a new type is added, along with this schema and both systems' DB CHECK constraints.

stop_loss_indicator_params.description: Only set when stop_loss_method='indicator' - shape depends on stop_loss_indicator_type (for 'ema': {"period": int}; for 'supertrend': {"period": int, "multiplier": number}).

target_percent.description: Independent of stop_loss_method - always a flat % from entry price. null means no target configured.

trailing_stop_enabled.description: Only meaningful when stop_loss_method is set. No trailing variant for target.

exit_condition.description: From the resolved Strategy - independent of stop_loss_method/target_percent/square-off. A single Condition (signal-engine's app/domain/generation/rule.py Term/Condition shape, the same one MultiConditionRuleConfig's own `conditions` list uses): {"interval": string, "left": Term, "operator": ">"|"<"|">="|"<=", "right": Term}, each Term {"kind": string, "field"?: string, "period"?: int, "offset_bars": int, "scale": number, "value"?: number}. Evaluated on every execution exit-monitor tick against fresh candle history at its own interval; closes the position outright (exit_reason='exit_condition') the first tick it evaluates true - e.g. 'close the BUY when 5min CCI(200) crosses back below +200', not expressible as a fixed distance from entry. null means unused. interval='daily' is rejected at Strategy save time (signal-engine's validate_exit_condition) - execution has no live per-tick way to evaluate a still-forming daily bar.

duplicate_signal_policy.description: From the resolved Strategy. Governs what happens when this symbol already has an OPEN position in the SAME direction as this order: 'skip' rejects the new order, 'add_position' opens an independent additional position (pyramiding).

counter_signal_policy.description: From the resolved Strategy. Governs what happens when this symbol already has an OPEN position in the OPPOSITE direction from this order: 'skip' leaves it open and untouched (this order is evaluated independently), 'close_and_flip' closes it (exit_reason='counter_signal') before this order is opened - takes effect synchronously at signal-intake time, ahead of that position's own stop-loss/target/square-off.

option_sl_scope.description: instrument_type='option' only, from the resolved Strategy - null for spot/future orders. 'combined' (default): one SL/target threshold on the combined (net debit) premium, the original Phase 4d design. 'individual': each leg gets its own SL/target computed from its own entry premium - whichever leg's own threshold trips first still closes the WHOLE group together (same atomic close as 'combined'), it only changes what triggers the close, never leaves one leg open while the other closes. Mathematically identical to 'combined' for a naked (1-leg) position - no separate handling needed there.

fixed_lots.description: From the resolved Strategy, every instrument_type (renamed from option_fixed_lots, which used to be options-only) - null if not set. When set, execution trades exactly this many LOTS instead of auto-sizing off capital_per_trade/risk_per_trade_pct - takes precedence over stop-loss-based (risk-%) sizing entirely, even when a stop-loss is also configured. The stop-loss price itself is still computed and stored as normal; only its role in sizing is bypassed. Number of lots, not raw underlying units - a no-op distinction for spot (lot_size is always 1 there) but real for futures/options. See docs/architecture.md.

use_margin.description: From the resolved Strategy. Only meaningful for segment='NSE'+horizon='positional'+instrument_type='spot' (harmlessly ignored otherwise). Opts this order into execution.accounts' platform-wide NSE leverage (Dhan MTF) and interest when the admin has configured leverage>1 there - false (default) always sizes/holds on cash regardless of that platform config. See docs/architecture.md.

owner_user_id.description: From the resolved Strategy's created_by (signal-generation.strategies.created_by, 2026-08-30) - whoever was logged in when the Strategy was created. null for a Strategy created with no bearer token, or any pre-existing Strategy from before this field existed - execution then keeps its original platform-wide behavior (Position.user_id=NULL, sizes against the shared execution.accounts row). When set, execution sizes/credits against THAT user's own per-user account (lazily created on first use, same as any other per-user account) and sets the resulting Position's user_id to it, so a Strategy-driven position is now visible/actionable to its own creator instead of only an admin. Distinct from execution.strategy_accounts.live_trading_user_id (whose real Dhan credentials place a REAL order for this strategy, if it's opted into live trading) - the two may name different people, or only one may be set.
